How to play the game of Class 1

Read this page once: it takes five minutes. After that you can play the game alone, without any explanation from the professor. Seven short animations, recorded from the game itself, show every step.

Start

Before you start

Three things to know · one minute
  1. Open the file IT505_Class01_GAME.html with a double click. It opens in your browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
  2. You do not need the internet to play. You need it only for the videos and the links.
  3. Your progress is kept in this browser, on this computer. Use the same browser next time, and your points are still there.
The game is formative. It gives you feedback only and does not count for your grade. A wrong answer costs a few points of the game, nothing else.

The game holds the whole of Class 1: three lessons in nine missions, the 49 slides with their notes, 25 flashcards, 18 questions, the first lab in eight animations, the videos, the links and the list of words.

1

The map

Where every visit starts
  • The top bar never moves: your level and your points are on the right, the menu is below the title.
  • The nine missions are grouped by lesson. They open one after the other; the next one has a red frame.
  • A grey mission is locked: finish the mission before it. The button Free play, at the bottom of the map, opens all missions at once.
  • Fold hides the missions of a lesson, Unfold shows them again.
2

A mission has three steps

Try · Name it · Use it — about three minutes for each mission

Every mission works in the same way. You do not read first and answer afterwards: you try first. The explanation comes when you have met the problem.

Step 1 — Try

  • Read the problem in the box with the red edge.
  • Answer on the page. A wrong answer is allowed: the message tells you what to look at.
  • When the problem is solved, the button Continue appears.

Step 2 — Name it

  • The coloured box gives the idea in two or three sentences.
  • Each title below it is one part of the lecture: click a title to unfold it, click again to fold it.
  • A chip such as Slide 10 opens the slide of the lecture with its notes. Back returns to your mission.
  • Take the time that you need here; there are no points to lose.

Step 3 — Use it

  • Answer a few short questions with the idea that you have just read.
  • After each answer you see why it is right or wrong. Press Next.
  • At the end you get your stars and your points, and the next mission opens.

Seven kinds of problem

The control changes from mission to mission; the instruction is always in the box with the red edge
KindWhat you doWhere
CalendarClick the days that answer the question.Mission 1
SliderMove the slider, then press Check.Mission 2
ButtonsClick the button of your answer; then Next.Missions 3, 6, 7 and 9, and every step “Use it”
TableClick the rows that are wrong.Mission 4
SwitchesSwitch rules on, then press Insert.Mission 5
Text boxChange the text of block 2, then press Recompute.Mission 8
OrderClick the steps in the right order: first, second, third.Mission 9, step “Use it”

6

Questions and answers

Seven frequent questions

I closed the page. Is my progress lost?

No. Open the same file in the same browser: your points are there. In a private window, or in a browser that blocks storage for local files, the progress lasts only until you close the page.

A mission is grey and I cannot open it.

Finish the mission before it. To revise one topic directly, press Free play at the bottom of the map.

I got one star. Can I do better?

Yes. Open the mission again and play it once more: the game keeps your best result.

Does the game count for my grade?

No. It is formative: it gives feedback only.

A video or a link does not open.

Videos and links need the internet. Everything else works without it.

How do I start again from zero?

Press Start the whole game again at the bottom of the map, twice.

Can I play on a telephone?

Yes, the page adapts to a small screen. A computer is more comfortable for Missions 4, 5 and 8, which show tables.
